deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript note for the EGA VII plan. It is page (29) of the typescript of SGA 4, Exposé VIII (Deligne/Grothendieck, 'Foncteurs fibres, supports, étude cohomologique des morphismes finis'), §7, apparently misfiled at the end of cote 48. The previous page, which belongs to the abelian-schemes plan, is unrelated.

Setting. X is a prescheme. Pt(X) is the category of geometric points of X, with specialization arrows as morphisms (defined in 7.6). For a geometric point ξ, the étale stalk F ↦ F_ξ is a fibre functor, i.e. a point of the étale topos. This gives the functor (*): Pt(X)° → Pt(X̃_ét).

Theorem 7.9. (*) identifies geometric points with specialization maps and fibre functors on the étale topos, contravariantly.

Sketch of part (a), full faithfulness.
1. For U étale over X, let U^∨ be evaluation at U: U^∨(F) = Hom(U,F) = F(U). Here U also denotes the sheaf it represents.
2. The stalk functor is a filtered colimit of such evaluations: ε_ξ ≅ colim_i X_i^∨. The X_i run over the affine étale neighbourhoods of ξ, indexed by a pseudo-filtrant category (refs 4.3, 4.5). In other words, the fibre functor is pro-represented by the system of étale neighbourhoods, whose limit is Spec of the strict henselization O^sh_{X,ξ}.
3. Hence, for any functor φ: X̃_ét → (Ens), Hom(ε_ξ, φ) ≅ lim_i Hom(X_i^∨, φ).
4. By Yoneda, Hom(X_i^∨, φ) ≅ φ(X_i).

The page stops here. The continuation, not shown, takes φ = ε_η. Then Hom(ε_ξ, ε_η) ≅ lim_i η-stalk of X_i ≅ the set of X-morphisms from the geometric point η to Spec O^sh_{X,ξ}, i.e. the specialization arrows between η and ξ. Part (b), essential surjectivity, would show that every point of X̃_ét comes from a geometric point, up to the universe caveats the text mentions.

Purpose: to describe the points of the étale topos. The text says explicitly that the theorem is not used later in the seminar, hence only a sketch.
errors: Variance looks inconsistent. The source is already written as Pt(X)°, yet the typed 'équivalence' was corrected by hand to 'anti-équivalence'. Whether this is right depends on the convention for morphisms of points versus morphisms of fibre functors, which are opposite. The hand correction suggests the authors themselves hesitated over the direction.

Notation clash: the letter X is reused for the base prescheme and for an object of X_ét ('Pour tout X ∈ Ob X_ét'), which is confusing but harmless. Hom(X,F) = F(X) tacitly identifies X with the sheaf it represents.

The index category of étale neighbourhoods is cofiltered as a category of schemes; it is filtered for the colimit of X_i^∨. The text's 'pseudo-filtrante' glosses over this direction, which is standard abuse.

ideas.what: Points of the étale topos of a scheme correspond to geometric points, and morphisms of points correspond to specialization maps
ideas.modern_name: Points of the étale topos; specialization of geometric points (Stacks Project, points of the étale site)

ideas.what: Stalk functor as a filtered colimit of evaluation functors at étale neighbourhoods (pro-representability by the strict henselization)
ideas.modern_name: Pro-representability of fibre functors; strict henselization

ideas.what: Yoneda: natural transformations from an evaluation functor U^∨ to φ correspond to φ(U)

missed.claim: Archival observation only. This sheet is a typescript page (29) of SGA 4 Exposé VIII (Theorem 7.9 on fibre functors of the étale topos), with a handwritten correction. It is filed in the folder 'Plan EGA VII : notes manuscrites' and is unrelated to the EGA VII plan on abelian schemes. The hand correction 'an+ti' records a convention decision on variance. No new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of SGA 4 VIII §7 (Theorem 7.9), a published and standard result with a routine pro-representability and Yoneda proof sketch. The only interest is archival: the page is misfiled, and a hand correction concerns variance.
transcription_corrections: 'an{+ti+}-équivalence': the letters 'ti' are handwritten over the typescript, giving 'anti-équivalence'.
Arrows typed as '--->' are ordinary functor arrows (→), not dashed rational maps; '⇝' for F ↦ F_ξ is correct.
The page number '(29' is the typescript pagination of SGA 4 VIII; the '5' at bottom left is the archive sheet number.
'certeine' is a typo in the original for 'certaine'.
Ŭ/X^∨ notation: the original writes both X^∨ and X̌ for the same evaluation functor.
